sources: Official list: Exophase, Grand Theft Auto VI (PSN) trophies — names, descriptions, grades, hidden flags.
PSNProfiles, Grand Theft Auto VI trophy list — PSN progress targets (counts) where a trophy has one.
notes: Hidden flags mark the spoiler-sensitive trophies (story missions, chapters and narrative moments). Missable flags are inferred from the official descriptions' wording and are labelled as inferred wherever they appear.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the Platinum itself: it unlocks automatically once the other 54 trophies are earned, so there is nothing separate to do for it. Treat it as the finish line of the roadmap below rather than a task: clear the story, the stranger strands, the activities and collectibles, then the 100% completion gold, and this follows.
trophies.tips: Work the roadmap phases in order; the Platinum pops with your final outstanding trophy, usually the 100% completion gold.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Story trophy for the opening mission, Gone Fishing, named directly in the official description. Play the campaign from the start and it unlocks as that mission ends; it cannot be skipped if you follow the story. Because it is the first mission, it is also a good moment to learn movement, driving and the wanted system before later trophies depend on them.
trophies.tips: No preparation is possible or needed; just finish the opening mission on any difficulty.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing Chapter 1 of the story. Keep playing the main missions in order and it unlocks at the chapter break. Story progress is linear here, so nothing in the description suggests a choice that could lock this out; if the game offers optional activities along the way, they can safely wait until after the chapter ends.
trophies.tips: Push main missions first in each chapter; side content stays available afterwards in past GTA-style design (expectation, not confirmed).
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing Chapter 2. As with Chapter 1, follow the main mission markers to the chapter's end. The chapter-based structure in the descriptions (Chapters 1 to 4, then a final mission) suggests a linear campaign spine, so treat this as unmissable story progress and use the chapter to unlock new areas and contacts that later activity trophies need.
trophies.tips: If a mission stalls you, lower-risk retries cost nothing but time; there is no difficulty trophy in the official list.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing Chapter 3. Continue the main story; the trophy lands at the chapter break. By mid-campaign, past Rockstar games have usually opened the full map and most activity types, so this is a natural point to start sampling activities for Master of None rather than leaving every side system to the endgame (pattern from GTA V and RDR2; an expectation, not a confirmed fact about this game).
trophies.tips: Start trying one of each activity type around now so no single system is left completely cold for the cleanup phase.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Awarded for finishing Chapter 4, the last numbered chapter before the finale. Follow the main missions to the chapter break. Before pushing past it, tidy up any stranger strands you have open: the descriptions give no point-of-no-return warning, but finales in past Rockstar games have sometimes reshaped the world state, so finishing open strands first is cheap insurance (expectation based on series patterns).
trophies.tips: Save in a separate slot before the final stretch so you keep a pre-finale world state to return to.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Gold trophy for completing the final mission and finishing the story. It is the campaign's endpoint, so everything story-related should be done or deliberately left for post-story cleanup before you take it on. The official description says nothing about multiple endings; if the finale presents a choice, the separate Choices trophy (Actions Speak Louder) is the one to watch, and a manual save beforehand protects both.
trophies.tips: Make a manual save before the final mission so any endgame choice can be revisited without replaying the campaign.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Story trophy for the mission Breakfast Run, named in the official description. It unlocks as that campaign mission ends, in story order. Mission-named trophies like this one are best treated as progress markers: if it has not popped when you expected, the mission simply has not been reached yet rather than failed.
trophies.tips: Just play the story; mission-completion trophies pop on the mission results screen in past Rockstar games (expectation).
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Story trophy for The Cartel Heist, named in the official description. Heists in this series are usually set-piece missions with preparation beats, so expect this one to arrive mid-story rather than as free-roam content. It unlocks on completion; performance medals or optional objectives are not mentioned in the description, so a clean finish is all that is required as far as the official text says.
trophies.tips: Stock up on armour and snacks before heist-style missions; survival, not style, is what a completion trophy checks.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Story trophy for the mission Child's Play, named in the official description. Play the campaign in order and it unlocks when the mission ends. Nothing in the wording suggests a performance condition, a choice or a collectible component, so treat it as an unmissable progress marker on the way to the chapter trophies.
trophies.tips: No special setup: follow the main mission chain and this follows.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Story trophy for the mission Headliners, named in the official description. It unlocks on completing that campaign mission. The all-caps name DWNFALL is the trophy's title, not an extra condition; the only requirement the official text states is finishing Headliners, so progress through the story is the whole guide.
trophies.tips: If you are trophy-hunting efficiently, let mission trophies accumulate naturally instead of hunting them one by one.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Story trophy for VCIA Takedown, named in the official description. VCIA is the airport authority in the game's fiction, and a separate bronze (Catch Me If You Can) also turns on an unscheduled departure at VCIA, so this area likely matters twice. Finish the mission for this trophy, and stay alert during any VCIA visit for the departure moment the other trophy wants.
trophies.tips: While at VCIA for this mission, explore the terminal area; the unscheduled-departure trophy is flagged as a possible one-time moment.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Story trophy for Operation Savage Glory, named in the official description. Complete that campaign mission to unlock it. The military flavour of the name suggests a loud, vehicle-heavy set piece; as with the other mission trophies, the official text asks only for completion, not for a medal, a time or a no-deaths run.
trophies.tips: Bring your best weapons and a full armour bar into overtly military missions; completion is the only stated bar.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Gold trophy for reaching 100% completion on the game's own completion counter. This is the long pole of the Platinum: in past Rockstar games the 100% checklist has covered story, stranger missions, hobbies and pastimes, collectibles and miscellaneous feats, and the official list here points the same way (stranger strands, activities, card sets, areas explored). Track the in-game percentage early so no category is left at zero until the end (the checklist split is an expectation from GTA V and RDR2 design).
trophies.tips: Open the in-game 100% checklist after Chapter 1 and chip at every category a little at a time; the last few percent are the slowest.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Silver trophy for completing 250 stunts. Stunt jumps and similar feats are repeatable world activities in this series, so this is a grind of accumulation rather than a skill gate: find stunt spots as you explore, clear them as you pass, and let the counter build across the whole playthrough instead of farming one spot at the end. PSN tracks the count toward 250, so you can check progress in the trophy card.
trophies.tips: Do stunts opportunistically while travelling between missions; 250 reached passively beats 250 farmed in one sitting.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each type of activity once. PSN's target, as listed with the official list, is 9 activity types, so the job is breadth, not mastery: the moment a new activity icon appears (races, fishing, arcade games, the shooting range and their kin), do one round of it and move on. Keep a note of which types you have sampled; the trophy pops when the last untouched type is tried.
trophies.tips: Sample each activity the first time the map shows it; this pairs naturally with exploring new areas for The Goodtime State.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Silver trophy for gold medals in all Shooting Range challenges; PSN's target is 42 challenges. This is a genuine skill trophy: learn each weapon class's challenge layout, prioritise accuracy chains over raw speed where the scoring rewards it, and retry immediately while the layout is fresh. Ranges usually unlock early and stay open, so spread attempts across the playthrough rather than forcing all 42 in one session (availability pattern from past games; an expectation).
trophies.tips: Gold one weapon class at a time and stop when frustrated; muscle memory for a challenge survives a break better than tilt does.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location; PSN's target is 14 locations. Winning, not just entering, is required, so learn each course's line over a couple of attempts and take the racing line through gates rather than chasing perfect speed. New locations likely appear as the map opens up, so check the race list again after each chapter (expectation from the series' activity rollout).
trophies.tips: Run a new course once slowly to learn it, then attack it; one win per location is enough, personal bests earn nothing extra.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word 'different' is the condition: repeating one easy race twenty times should not count, so work across the race list and keep a tally of which events you have actually won. Races across vehicle classes likely all count toward the twenty (the description does not limit the class), so mix land, sea and air events as they unlock.
trophies.tips: Tick off wins in the tracker notes as you go; near the end, target the shortest unwon races first.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a named character, so this is a scripted challenge rather than open fishing: find Cal's challenge, learn the fishing timing the game teaches, and out-catch him. If fishing has a skill element (bait, location, time of day), the challenge itself usually fixes the conditions, so persistence and learning the reeling rhythm are the levers you control (challenge structure is an expectation; the official text only names the opponent and the contest).
trophies.tips: Practise free fishing first if the game allows it, so the challenge attempt is not also your tutorial.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete an arcade game. Find an arcade cabinet or machine in the world, play one game through to its completion condition rather than just starting it, and the trophy unlocks. This is one of the cheapest bronzes on the list: a single finished arcade game, with no score target stated in the official description.
trophies.tips: Do this the first time you pass an arcade; it takes minutes and banks progress toward Master of None at the same time.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Andy, one of the named contacts whose strands make up the strangers content. Work Andy's mission chain whenever it appears until no more of his markers show; the trophy lands on the last one. Stranger strands in this series can be spread across chapters, so if Andy goes quiet, progress the story and check back (availability pattern from GTA V and RDR2; an expectation).
trophies.tips: Finish each contact's whole strand in one push once the final mission is available, so strands do not get lost among map icons.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Kenton. Follow Kenton's strand from its first marker to its last mission; the trophy unlocks at the strand's end. Kenton is also the name attached to the bowling alley in another trophy (Let's Go Bowling, at Kolt & Associates' alley), so time spent around Kenton's places may serve two trophies; the official texts do not confirm a link, so treat that as a lead, not a fact.
trophies.tips: When Kenton's strand opens, clear it promptly; strand-givers in past games occasionally moved or paused between chapters (expectation).
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Billy. Billy's strand is one of the named-contact chains feeding the Strangers & Freaks silver, which needs eight strands finished. Play Billy's missions as they surface and the bronze lands on the final one. If the strand seems to end early, it may resume after story progress; check again after each chapter (series pattern; an expectation).
trophies.tips: Count finished strands toward the eight Strangers & Freaks needs; Billy is one of them.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Silver trophy for completing 8 mission strands for strangers across Leonida. The named-contact bronzes (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and their kin) are strands of exactly this kind, so this silver is earned by finishing those chains rather than by separate content: complete eight full strands, start to finish. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, so half-finished chains are the usual reason this lags behind.
trophies.tips: Keep a strand tally in your notes; when this sits unfinished late, the fix is almost always one contact's final mission still waiting.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Randy, whose strand is literally titled Supply & Demand as its own trophy for Tyrone's chain-end naming pattern shows these contacts carry the side economy of Leonida. Play Randy's missions through to the last one. As with the other contacts, if the chain pauses, advance the story and return; strands in this series commonly gate their later beats behind campaign progress (expectation).
trophies.tips: Do Randy's final mission as soon as it appears so the strand counts toward Strangers & Freaks without a cleanup hunt.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission for Tyrone. Tyrone's chain is one of the eight strands the Strangers & Freaks silver wants, so finishing it banks both this bronze and a strand of progress. Follow his markers to the end of the chain; nothing in the official description adds a performance condition, so completion alone is the requirement as written.
trophies.tips: Strand finales often pay well in-game; use the cash toward the spending and garage trophies.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida; PSN's target is 18 spots. This is a collectible-style sweep: meditation spots are fixed world locations, so the work is finding and visiting all eighteen. Spots in scenic or remote places are the ones players miss, so sweep region by region alongside area exploration for The Goodtime State, and tick spots off as you find them so the last two are not a statewide guessing game.
trophies.tips: Pair this with exploration: whenever you open a new area, look for its quiet scenic spot before leaving.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret is a named contact, so expect a specific hunt rather than generic wildlife kills: take Bret's request, track the one unique animal it names, and bring it down. Unique-animal hunts in this series usually add a tracking or bait step and a tougher target than ambient wildlife (an expectation from RDR2's legendary animals pattern); go in with a suitable long-range weapon and full health.
trophies.tips: Save before the hunt; a unique target that escapes or is ruined may need a reload rather than a respawn (precaution, not confirmed).
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Silver trophy for completing 3 collectible card sets. Cards are world collectibles grouped into sets, so this needs systematic collecting rather than luck: pick up every card you pass, and once sets start completing, target the missing cards of your nearest set first instead of spreading thin. Three full sets, not three cards, is the bar, so expect this to be a mid-to-late cleanup task once most of the map is known.
trophies.tips: Finish one set at a time; a set at 90% is worth more than three sets at 30% when you are choosing where to travel.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Silver trophy for using WAiNK It at 100 locations; PSN tracks the count to 100. Whatever WAiNK It proves to be in-world, the shape is clear from the description: a repeatable location-based action scattered across Leonida, done once per location. Treat it like a collectible sweep: do it whenever you encounter a new spot, keep the tally moving during exploration, and save the final mop-up for when the map is fully open.
trophies.tips: Never leave a new location without checking for this; the last 20 locations are far slower to hunt than the first 80 are to stumble on.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's bite-size objectives; fifty completions is a breadth grind across systems rather than depth in one. Sample challenges from every category the game offers (driving, combat, exploration and activity challenges in past games), because easy early challenges in many categories add up faster than hard late ones in a single category (category structure is an expectation; the official text only fixes the count).
trophies.tips: Keep a running count and favour short challenges while travelling; this pairs well with Master of None's activity sampling.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner present and escape the heat. The partner is the game's second protagonist, so this is a co-presence feat, not an online one as far as the official text shows: raise a 4-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear. The risk is escalation, so plan the escape route (alleys, water, a vehicle swap) before you earn the fourth star.
trophies.tips: Start the trouble somewhere with cover and an exit; losing the cops is about breaking sightlines, not outrunning them.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level. Three robberies in one continuous wanted run: the wanted level must stay alive between shops, so dawdling until the heat dies fails the attempt even though escaping would be safer. Pick three shops close together, move fast between them, and keep your partner alongside throughout, as the description requires their presence.
trophies.tips: Scout a tight cluster of shops first and rob them in a planned loop; travel time between shops is where runs die.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Discovery in this series usually means entering or encountering a vehicle model for the first time, so variety is the whole job: get into cars, bikes, boats and aircraft you have not used, especially parked rarities in rich districts, docks and airfields. One hundred distinct vehicles is a big slice of the vehicle list, so start early and treat every new model as progress (the enter-to-discover mechanic is the series pattern; an expectation).
trophies.tips: Steal or board anything unfamiliar on sight; the airport, marina and wealthy suburbs are the densest sources of new models.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the game's slow-motion combat ability, so this is about setup: trigger it only when at least five enemies are in reach and line of sight, then drop them before the meter ends. Crowded firefights in missions are the natural chance; in free roam, manufacture one by drawing a group together before you activate the ability.
trophies.tips: Wait for a cluster, not a trickle: five targets visible at activation is the difference between a pop and a near miss.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the airport. FLAGGED MISSABLE (inferred): the wording sounds like a specific story-moment opportunity rather than a repeatable free-roam action, and VCIA features in the story mission VCIA Takedown, so the chance may exist only while you are there for the plot. When any VCIA sequence gives you an aircraft, an opening or an unexpected way out, take it instead of following the scripted exit, and keep a save from before the mission so you can retry the moment.
trophies.tips: Save before VCIA story beats; if a departure prompt or vehicle appears off-script, take it first and ask questions after.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description, 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos', points at Rhino tanks: expect a story or set-piece encounter with military armour rather than a free-roam feat, though the official text is too cryptic to pin the exact trigger. When Rhinos appear, engage with the encounter as presented (survive it, use one, or destroy one, as the scene demands) and the trophy should follow the encounter's resolution. Because the wording is a joke rather than an instruction, treat any Rhino set piece as the moment and do not rush past it.
trophies.tips: If a mission puts you near or in a Rhino, experiment before leaving the area; cryptic trophies usually attach to the obvious set piece.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. A stealth robbery: enter, take the goods and get out without the alarm state or witnesses flagging you as detected. Prepare by scoping the store first, choosing a quiet moment, and controlling witnesses the way the game's robbery systems allow; if detection triggers, the clean approach is to abandon the attempt and return later rather than completing a loud robbery that cannot count (detection rules are inferred from the wording; the official text states only the condition).
trophies.tips: Attempt this in a low-traffic moment with an escape vehicle ready; a failed loud robbery costs nothing but time if stores reset.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Silver trophy for robbing 5 bank vaults and escaping. Five separate vault robberies, each closed out by a successful escape, so this is repeatable heist content rather than one story beat: learn one vault's routine, then work through the others as they become available. Escaping is part of the condition, so a robbery that ends in arrest or death should not count; plan the getaway before you crack the vault.
trophies.tips: Master the escape first (route, vehicle swap, hiding spot); the vault itself is the easy half once the getaway is routine.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks are roaming world targets in this series: stop one, open it, take the cash and lose the heat. The description needs one successful truck robbery with an escape, so pick your moment (a truck away from heavy police presence), bring something that can force it open, and have the escape planned before you start (the roaming-truck pattern is from past games; an expectation).
trophies.tips: Do not start on a truck near a police station; the escape condition is what turns a robbery into this trophy.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida; PSN's target is 52 areas. Exploration trophies in this series credit entering each named area, so this is a map-completion sweep: travel everywhere, including water, islands and rural corners that missions never visit. Leave it until vehicles and fast travel are fully available, then sweep the map region by region against the in-game map so no unnamed pocket survives (area-credit mechanics are the series pattern; an expectation).
trophies.tips: Work the coastline and islands deliberately; land areas open naturally, but offshore areas are the classic last percent.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang; PSN's target is 9 gangs. One operation per gang, nine gangs total: as you identify each gang's territory and operations, rob one of theirs and note which gangs are covered. The risk is repetition without coverage, robbing the same two gangs repeatedly, so keep the gang tally in your notes from the first robbery onward.
trophies.tips: When you enter new turf, find its gang operation early; new gangs appear with new areas as the map opens.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. FLAGGED MISSABLE (inferred): the title, 'In The Beginning…', ties this to an early-game moment, and small scene trophies like this in past Rockstar games have sometimes been attached to a specific story window rather than a permanently available interaction. If an early Ocean Beach scene offers a drink or a pause, take it; if cocktail spots exist in free roam, any beach bar with a view is worth trying whenever you pass (the free-roam fallback is a hope, not a confirmed fact).
trophies.tips: In the opening hours, linger at Ocean Beach and accept any drink prompt; do not rush the first beach scene.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. FLAGGED MISSABLE (inferred): driving out through showroom glass reads as a scripted story set piece, the kind of moment a mission stages once. When a mission puts you inside a vehicle showroom with a car available, drive out through the window rather than the door or a scripted exit, whatever the marker suggests. Keeping a save before showroom-adjacent missions protects the attempt.
trophies.tips: Inside any showroom during a mission, get in the car and aim for the glass; 'classic style' means the window, not the exit.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. The trophy's name riffs on the series' famous bowling invitations, and the description points at a bowling activity at one named alley: go there, bowl, and complete the follow-through the activity asks for (a full game is the safe interpretation of 'follow-through' until the game shows otherwise). Bowling also counts as an activity type, so this visit can serve Master of None too.
trophies.tips: Play a complete game rather than a single frame; completion-style wording usually means finishing the activity.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The description, 'A partnership with mass appeal', is deliberately vague: it points at a moment involving the two protagonists and public attention, but the official text does not say where or when. Treat it as a watch-for-it trophy: when a story or side scene puts the partnership on display (a crowd, cameras, a public stunt), lean into it rather than skipping the scene. If it has not popped by the endgame, the honest position is that its trigger is a specific scene; replaying chapter content, if the game allows it, is the fallback (an expectation, not a confirmed route).
trophies.tips: Never skip partnership cutscenes; vague scene trophies attach to moments you cannot identify in advance.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Choices made (for better or worse). FLAGGED MISSABLE (inferred): a trophy built on choices implies branching moments, and choices are where content can be locked out; PSN also tracks a count toward 500, so choices appear to be a tracked, repeatable statistic as well as story beats. Play naturally and make decisions rather than avoiding them, keep manual saves before big story decisions so alternate outcomes stay reachable, and if the count matters, know that everyday decisions appear to feed it too (the 500 target is PSN's, listed with the official list).
trophies.tips: Save before any decision the game presents as weighty; you protect this trophy and every strand that might depend on the outcome.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm: succeed at something on the second attempt after failing the first. FLAGGED MISSABLE (inferred): if this attaches to a specific one-time event, succeeding first try could pass it by, so when a distinctive challenge or event appears for the first time, a deliberate early failure is the cautious play before you commit to winning it. If instead it tracks any fail-then-succeed pair, it will pop naturally the first time you retry anything successfully; either way, never treat a first failure as wasted time (the trigger is not stated in the official text, so this is inference from its wording).
trophies.tips: When something new and one-off-feeling appears, fail it once on purpose, then succeed; that sequence satisfies both readings of the wording.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? A trophy for witnessing something strange: an odd event, sighting or occurrence somewhere in Leonida. Strange-event trophies in open worlds usually attach to scripted oddities (remote locations, night-time encounters, odd strangers), so explore off the main paths, especially at night and in rural or coastal corners, and stop to watch when something unusual starts rather than driving through it (event placement is an expectation; the official text only promises strangeness).
trophies.tips: Investigate anything that looks staged-weird: lights, crowds, abandoned scenes. These trophies reward curiosity, not speed.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by: knock a pedestrian down by striking them from a moving vehicle with a melee attack, the 'bowling' being the victim's fall. Set it up somewhere with pedestrians and room to drive: approach at moderate speed, swing as you pass, and make sure the hit connects from the vehicle rather than after dismounting. It may take a few passes to learn the timing; no wanted-level or location condition is stated.
trophies.tips: Slow passes beat fast ones: you need contact with the swing, and a near miss at speed teaches nothing.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. A money grind with a specific channel: only marked bills washed through contacts count, not general income, so once the laundering route opens (likely through the side-economy contacts), route every marked bill you get through it and track the laundered total against the quarter-million bar. Expect this to finish late; it is paced like an endgame economy trophy.
trophies.tips: Never sell or spend marked bills another way once laundering exists; every unwashed bill is progress thrown away.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Cumulative spending anywhere in the economy counts, so this arrives naturally if you buy vehicles, weapons, clothes and property upgrades instead of hoarding cash. There is no reason to farm it early; if it is somehow still short in the cleanup phase, buying garage stock and shop goods closes the gap quickly. Note the spending must be across shops, so one giant non-shop purchase may not feed it (the wording's limit, read literally).
trophies.tips: Buy what you actually want all game long; check this only in cleanup, and top it up with shop purchases if it lags.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties; PSN's target is 8 garages. A money-and-map trophy: garages are bought properties spread across Leonida, so you need both the cash and the locations found. Buy them as you encounter them if funds allow, or sweep them in cleanup once the economy trophies have filled your wallet; either way, eight purchases is the whole requirement as the official text states it.
trophies.tips: Garages double as vehicle storage, so buying early is useful, not just progress; do not leave all eight to the endgame bill.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Use the in-game app to register vehicles until the count reaches ten: whenever you acquire a vehicle you intend to keep, register it there and then rather than batching later. Ten is a small target that fills naturally if registering becomes a habit from your first owned vehicles (the app's exact mechanics are not described in the official text, so follow its in-game prompts).
trophies.tips: Register every keeper vehicle the moment you get it; ten registrations sneak up fast when it is a habit.
trophies.source: Official trophy description (PS5 list via Exophase; PSN target via PSNProfiles). Guide: original text; inferences labelled.
